entries.text: Facade trim (timbers, window frames, muntins) must protrude slightly proud of the wall face (~0.15 studs) or it visually vanishes into the wall - check with a first capture_angles pass before detailing further.

Author idle loops as ABSOLUTE full-body keyposes (unlisted joints identity) with the first keyframe re-snapshotted as the last, then verify loop closure numerically (joint-delta between first/last == 0) instead of eyeballing the filmstrip.
Before capture_animation review, temporarily relocate the rig to clear ground with readable colors (then restore position/colors/pose) so filmstrip frames aren't obscured by scene props.

Ground generated/cloned models by computing the bounding-box bottom and offsetting to terrain height, and rescale Cube outputs by setting MeshPart.Size directly since Model:ScaleTo can silently no-op on them.

When dressing a large set-piece, place all props relative to one arena center/radius (torches at fractional radius, perimeter ring with a deliberate gate gap) so composition stays coherent and verifiable from orbit captures.

Load use_rubric(gui)+use_build_guide(gui) BEFORE laying out any ScreenGui and scaffold the rubric's structural baseline first (fullscreen governing root, scale-based sizing with AnchorPoints, a central role-based palette module, a padding system, constraints/TextScaled) - styling an ad-hoc offset layout and evaluating afterward guarantees baseline fails that require a rebuild.

A clean capture/playtest render is visual-presence evidence only, not quality evidence - run evaluate(category) as the pass gate before recording a rung as verified, and bake interaction feedback (hover/press states, tweened panel transitions) into every button/panel at creation time rather than as a polish pass.

Cube-generated weapon meshes can ship an order of magnitude oversized (31 studs here) - rescale MeshPart.Size to hand scale (~2.5-4 studs) immediately after generate_mesh, BEFORE any grip fitting or visual judging, since grip offsets and filmstrip reads are invalid at the wrong scale.

Choose the bind_behavior windup/active timings FIRST and author the use clip's keypose times to land the strike inside that window (e.g. strike keyframe at ~windup+active midpoint), so animation and hit window match without a rework pass.
Build wall openings as real geometry (pier+lintel+sill segments) instead of decals so doors/windows read as true voids from every angle and pass scale checks against the 5-stud character.
After assembling angled roof geometry, capture from a LOW angle specifically to catch parts left floating at the wall-top junction (eave/gable posts) before calling the build done.

Author idle loops as a palindromic keypose sequence (A-B-A-C-D-C-A) so the first and last keyframes are byte-identical, then verify seamlessness numerically by diffing first-vs-last pose transforms instead of eyeballing the filmstrip.

Prevent foot-slide in weight-shift idles by counter-rotating the ankles against the hip/waist roll and never keying foot translation, then verify by asserting foot/lower-leg pose transforms are constant across every keyframe.

Run an interim evaluate/wide-framing capture checkpoint right after the lighting/atmosphere pass and again before dressing is declared done - close-up captures alone can pass while the grader's full-world framing (which includes the plane edge, skirt, and post effects) fails all baselines.

Match set-extension scale to composition: keep the dressed set a dominant fraction of the visible ground plane and give the world edge irregular sculpted falloff, verifying from the widest capture distance rather than only arena-radius shots.
A mechanic change (4a6ff3b69f) was auto-reverted after the next same-family cycle regressed - re-diagnose from scratch before re-attempting that fix.

Rotated roof planes are sign-fragile: after placing them, assert numerically in edit that the ridge/center Y is HIGHER than the eave edges and that each plane's underside touches the wall-top Y (bbox/vertex probe), since raycast-through-the-door checks say nothing about roof orientation or seating.

When the capture pipeline is down, geometric checks must cover every orientation-sensitive assembly (slope direction, part contact/gaps) or the build should be flagged unverified rather than passed to VERIFY on doorway/bbox probes alone.

Probe viewport health FIRST (take two captures and frame-diff them; byte-identical frames = frozen/foreign view) before starting any cycle whose verify oracle is visual, so the build isn't authored against an unrenderable capture pipeline.

Author loop clips as a palindromic keypose sequence (A-B-A-C-D-C-A) and verify numerically that first-vs-last pose diff is 0.0 and no leg joint or Pose translation is keyed - this makes seam pops and foot-slide structurally impossible without needing playback.

Before starting any visually-verified build, health-check the capture pipeline with a frame-diffed shot of a known high-contrast test part (e.g. a giant neon block dead-center), and if it renders blank, mark the cycle UNVERIFIED up front rather than substituting geometry probes for the visual oracle at the end.

When the visual oracle is unavailable, still bank the build with numeric per-part world-extent checks (floating/buried tests, radius falloff, recess depths) plus an explicit re-capture handoff note, so the geometry work survives and only the visual pass is deferred.

Decorative overlays (accent stripes, glows) must be parented OUTSIDE any UIListLayout container - a layout treats every GuiObject child as a list item, so anchor them to the ScreenGui root or a layout-free sibling frame.
Preview a StarterGui menu via a temporary CoreGui clone to verify layout in edit mode, then delete the preview before playtesting so the shipped StarterGui copy stays the single source of truth.

After fitting a Tool.Grip, verify numerically in edit - probe the world positions of blade tip and pommel relative to the fist and assert the tip is the FAR end - because filmstrip/capture judging alone cannot distinguish blade-up from blade-reversed on a slender weapon.

When a grip fix flips orientation by rotation (e.g. rx -90), re-check the offset SIGN against the mesh's handle axis before binding behavior/hitbox: the same |offset| on the wrong side puts the palm mid-blade while the silhouette still reads plausible.
Before siting a new structure, probe the bounding boxes of existing large occupiers (GetExtentsSize on big Models) and pick genuinely clear ground - don't trust visually-empty coordinates.

Build wall openings by segmenting the wall into sill/header/side parts around each opening instead of boolean cuts, and verify roof wedge/slab orientation with an early capture_angles pass since pitched geometry easily assembles inverted.

For idle loops, prevent foot-slide structurally by giving every keyframe the exact same leg-joint pose table (never re-posing legs per key), so planted feet are guaranteed by construction instead of by visual inspection.

Guarantee a seamless loop by re-applying the first keypose's stored pose table verbatim at the final keyframe time, then verifying first==last numerically (0-degree joint deltas) in addition to filmstrip review.

Before siting a new scene, probe existing occupiers' bounding boxes in edit and pick clear ground coordinates so the build never collides with foreign parts - then probe any stray-colored parts afterward to confirm they lie outside your container.

Verify environments with ground-level character-height captures in addition to orbit shots - orbits confirm layout but only eye-level frames prove scale, silhouette, and readability at gameplay distance.

Before trusting a GUI capture, identify and exclude foreign overlays (e.g. leftover probe/debug guis) in the shot — clean up or hide stray ScreenGuis first so verification judges only the build under test.

When playtest_eval is unavailable, a GUI oracle can still be closed fully via capture-confirmed interaction states (panel visible, toggle text flipped, dismiss animation completed) plus clean playtest_logs — design GUI verify plans around visible state changes rather than server eval.

When CaptureService yields no screenshots, verify grips and mesh scale numerically in edit (part.Size extents vs the 5-stud character, world-space blade-axis/end-point math from Tool.Grip) instead of skipping visual gates.
Probe capture availability at cycle start and record the degraded-verification mode in the build notes, so downstream verify stages know to run numeric/playtest checks instead of waiting on images.

Build openings by assembling walls as segments around door/window gaps from the start rather than carving solid walls afterward, and frame each opening with protruding trim so it reads at capture distance.

WedgePart roof gables only read correctly at yaw 0/180 relative to the roof ridge (other yaws read as fins) - set gable orientation from the ridge axis and confirm with a multi-angle capture round before detailing.
Close a looping clip by re-snapshotting the exact first keypose as the final keyframe (and diff the two numerically) instead of hand-matching angles - it guarantees a seamless loop seam.

Prevent foot-slide in weight-shift idles at author time by using only Motor6D rotations with hips/ankles counter-rotated (keeping subtle motion in a ~2-7 degree band), then confirm planted feet from two filmstrip angles rather than one.
